newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arab Bank demand boosts Jordanian stocks.
newsitem.headline: Arab Bank demand boosts Jordanian stocks.

text.p: Strong demand for shares in Arab Bank pushed up the official Jordanian stock exchange index in otherwise quiet trade on Wednesday.

Most stocks fell on the last trading day of the week but Arab Bank, which accounts for almost a third of total bourse capitalisation, drove the index up after it gained six dinars to 270 dinars in trade worth 246,000 dinars.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.85 percent to 162.39 points in trade worth 828,000 dinars ($1.17 million).

Broker Ibrahim Odeh of Wataniyeh Financial Services said the strong local demand was fuelled by expectations that the bank would call an extraordinary general assembly later this month to discuss raising its capital and issuing bonus shares.
Residual optimism over government plans to lift a 50 percent foreign stock ownership ceiling was also having a positive effect, he said.
Jordan Phosphate Mines also rose, backed by foreign demand, by 0.1 dinar to 4.10 dinars in healthy trade worth over 100,000 dinars.
The phosphate and banking gains helped to outweigh falls in 20 stocks on Wednesday. Just 11 stocks rose while 13 traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose a marginal 0.02 percent to 80.53 points, 3.43 percent down from the start of the year.
